claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater plastic strain than pure tungsten at high temperature.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater toughness than pure tungsten at high temperature.
Chemical complexity stabilizes refined grains and heterogeneous interfaces in WTaTiVZr.
The stabilized fine-scale features improve grain-boundary mediation of dislocation motion.
Improved grain-boundary mediation reduces crack nucleation and propagation.
The as-synthesized equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy has a homogeneous multiphase microstructure with fine-scale grain boundaries.
Commercially used pure tungsten is polycrystalline.
Grain boundaries and interphase interfaces in WTaTiVZr are established by its chemical complexity.
The constituent elements of WTaTiVZr are refractory and low-activation elements.
The refined, chemically heterogeneous WTaTiVZr microstructure enhances dislocation absorption and motion along grain boundaries.
The WTaTiVZr microstructure impedes rapid crack propagation.
Pure tungsten has a coarse-grained, homogeneous structure relative to WTaTiVZr.
The coarse-grained, homogeneous structure of pure tungsten makes it more prone to brittle failure under high-temperature stress.
At approximately 1200–1400°C, dislocation-mediated plasticity will dominate the mechanical response.
At lower temperatures, brittle-phase effects or other mechanisms may confound the response.
Prior observations show improved creep resistance in similar refractory high-entropy alloys.
Prior observations show improved corrosion resistance in similar refractory high-entropy alloys.

contradictions.description: The initial state describes WTaTiVZr as having a homogeneous microstructure, whereas the mechanism describes its operative microstructure as chemically heterogeneous; the intended meaning of homogeneity is not clarified.
